canonical.codes: minted pairing codes are replaced by C0DE<28-digit index> (1-based by first appearance in a case); Go draws 20 random bytes, base32-hex, 32 characters of [0-9A-V]
canonical.device_ids: device ids are replaced by dev-<16-digit hex index>; Go draws 8 random bytes (dev- plus 16 lower-case hex digits)
canonical.expires_at: 2026-01-02T03:09:05.123456789Z (asserted to be within 3 s of now plus the code lifetime, or plus the session lifetime for an enrolment)
canonical.queue_ids: request ids are replaced by apr-a<11-digit index>
canonical.tokens: device bearer tokens are replaced by T0KE<28-digit index>; same shape as codes

scope.cooldown_end: the end of the 30 s failure cooldown is not recorded (it would need a 30 s sleep); the Rust TokenStore pins it with an injected clock (symvault-sync pairing tests)
scope.mounting: the Go server mounts the four handlers on a ServeMux; the generator rebuilds that mux and pins the mounting source lines (mounting)
scope.non_loopback: cases flagged non_loopback_peer use a loopback predicate that refuses every peer, because a non-loopback TCP peer cannot be produced portably; the replay answers them through the handler function with a documentation-range peer address
scope.not_recorded: HEAD requests, TLS/mTLS (owned by HTTP-001..004 fixtures), peers other than loopback over a real socket and request bodies that are not UTF-8
scope.rate_limit: serverbootstrap wraps both enrolment routes in auth.RateLimiterMiddleware (default 60 requests/minute/IP); this recording drives the handlers on a bare mux, so no throttling is recorded here and the replay disables the Rust limiter (rate_limit 0); throttling of the enrolment routes is recorded by http002ratelimitgen
scope.sessions_after: store_after is read back from the persisted device-sessions.json through a fresh store: names, public keys and revocation; the raw bearer token is asserted absent from the file
scope.timing: code lifetime cases use a 300 ms lifetime and a 700 ms pause; proof windows use +-20 s (accepted) and +-35 s (refused) so the second boundary cannot flip a result
scope.transport: raw HTTP/1.1 over a loopback TCP listener serving the Go http.ServeMux; only Content-Type, X-Content-Type-Options and Location response headers are contract, Date/Content-Length/Connection are HTTP-library artefacts

cases.description: the request body, query string and content type play no part
the mux matches the exact path only; unclean paths are redirected, escaped hyphens decode
a minted code is exchanged for a device id and a bearer token the approval API accepts; the session is persisted by hash
a code redeems once; a second code is independent
401 for a code that was never minted, or is not exactly a minted code
strings.TrimSpace on the code: ASCII and Unicode spaces are trimmed, a zero-width space is not
an absent, empty, blank or null code is 400 and consumes nothing
400 malformed request body for anything the JSON decoder rejects, including a wrongly typed field, which consumes nothing
encoding/json semantics: unknown keys ignored, keys match case-insensitively, the last duplicate wins, only the first value is read, null leaves a field alone
the device name is stored verbatim (empty names omitted from the file); public_key stays empty
any method but POST is the handler's NotFound and consumes nothing
the mux matches the exact path only; the query string is ignored
a code past its lifetime is refused (and removed); a fresh code still works
five failures in a row put the store into a global cooldown in which even a valid code is refused (and kept); minting stays possible
a successful redemption clears the failure counter; four failures are tolerated every time
an expired code is a failed attempt; five of them start the cooldown
the enrolled bearer authorises the device approval API; decided_by is the new device id
every redemption yields a distinct device id and token; revoking one device (a second store instance) leaves the other working
Go reads only the first JSON value and sets no body limit: a body above one MiB is served
